title: Risk management approach, risk register, roles and principles
blurb: Explain the purpose of the risk management approach and the risk register, who does what on risk, and how the risk practice supports the principles.
question: The project manager wants to record the probability scales and the procedure the team will follow for risk. Should these go in the risk register or the risk management approach?

teach.body: Formally: the risk management approach describes how risk will be managed on the project, including the specific procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities to be applied. The risk register maintains a record of identified risks related to the project, including their status and history. In plain English: the approach is the rulebook; the register is the list of actual risks.

teach.caption: Writing a specific risk into the approach is a classic Practitioner wrong answer.

head: Heading
Example entry
teach.caption: Other headings can include identifier, author, date registered, category, probability and status. Exposure for a single risk is not a heading.

teach.body: Because the approach is the rulebook, it is where you find things like the risk procedure, tools and techniques, the scales for probability, impact and proximity, risk and response categories, early warning indicators, reporting and timing, roles and responsibilities, risk tolerance and how the risk budget is used. It is shaped by the business's own policies and standards, and is approved by the board in directing a project.

head: Role
Focus on risk
rows: Risk management policy and risk appetite
Sets risk tolerance; approves the approach
Creates approach and register; manages risks

Board approves the risk management approach
Capture and assess new risks; escalate if needed

How risk supports it

Risk tolerance set and escalated if breached
Risks reviewed at each stage boundary

teach.h: Worked scenario: a wind-farm grid connection
teach.body: At Northcape Energy, project manager Aisha Bello writes the risk management approach during initiation: a five-point probability scale, risk categories and a monthly review. Project support officer Liam Doyle sets up the risk register. When team manager Rhona Kerr finds that cable deliveries may slip, she notifies Aisha, who has it registered with its cause, event, effect, proximity, impact, response, owner and action owner. The board approves the approach as part of the PID.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) The risk management approach holds the PROCEDURE, scales and responsibilities; it holds NO specific risks. (2) The risk register holds specific threats AND opportunities, with status and history. (3) A team manager reports new risks to the project manager, not directly to the board. (4) Exposure for a single risk is not a register heading.

items: Risk management approach (PID): how risk will be managed; procedures, techniques, standards, responsibilities.
Risk register (project log): identified risks with status and history; threats and opportunities.
Register headings include description, proximity, impact, response, risk owner, risk action owner.
Business sets appetite; board sets tolerance and approves the approach; PM creates both products.
Risk supports the principles, for example aggregated risk in the business case and risk tolerance for manage by exception.

summary: You can now explain that the risk management approach describes how risk will be managed, while the risk register records the specific risks with their status and history. You can also say who does what on risk and how the risk practice supports the principles.

A.q: What is the purpose of the risk management approach?
options: To record identified risks with their status and history
To describe how changes to the baseline will be controlled
To summarize the risks for the board at each stage end
To describe how risk will be managed on the project
A.why: The risk management approach describes how risk will be managed, including procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities (9.5).

whyNot.1: That is the issue management approach.
whyNot.2: Stage-end summaries go in the end stage report.

A.q: What is the purpose of the risk register?
options: To describe the risk procedure and the scales used
To set the risk tolerance for each stage of the project
To record identified risks, with their status and history
To record lessons about risk for future projects
A.why: The risk register maintains a record of identified risks, including their status and history.

whyNot.0: That is the risk management approach.
whyNot.1: Tolerances are set by the board; the register records risks.
whyNot.3: Lessons go in the lessons log.

A.q: Which role decides the risk appetite?
A.why: Risk appetite is determined by the business and applied by the project board.

whyNot.1: The board applies the appetite by setting risk tolerance.
whyNot.2: The project manager manages risks within tolerance.
whyNot.3: Assurance reviews risk management practice for the board.

B.q:
Which two items belong in the risk management approach rather than the risk register?
1. The scales used to rate probability and impact.
2. A threat that the supplier may go into administration.
3. The procedure to follow when a new risk is found.
4. The name of the owner of a specific opportunity.
B.why: Scales (1) and the procedure (3) describe how risk is managed, so they belong in the approach.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is a specific risk, which goes in the register.
whyNot.1: Both are about specific risks, which belong in the register.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is about a specific risk, recorded in the register.

B.q: A team manager identifies a new threat to their work package. What should they do?
options: Raise an exception report to the board
Ask the business layer for more budget
B.why: In managing product delivery, team managers notify the project manager of new issues, risks or lessons.

whyNot.1: Team managers do not report to the board, and a new threat is not by itself an exception.
whyNot.2: The approach holds the procedure, not specific risks.
whyNot.3: Team managers do not escalate to the business layer.

B.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The risk [?] is part of the project log.
B.why: The project log contains the daily log, lessons log, issue, risk, quality and product registers.

whyNot.0: The risk management approach is part of the PID.
whyNot.1: The risk budget is part of a plan's budget.
whyNot.3: Risk tolerance is set by the board and documented in plans and approaches.

C.q: Which management product is approved by the project board in directing a project, and where is it held?
options: The risk register; in the project log
The risk management approach; in the PID
The risk register; in the PID
The risk management approach; in the project log
C.why: The board approves the risk management approach in directing a project; it is part of the PID.

whyNot.0: The register is in the project log, but it is maintained, not approved by the board.
whyNot.2: The register belongs to the project log, not the PID.
whyNot.3: The approach is part of the PID, not the project log.

C.q: During initiation, a draft risk management approach lists 'the planning permission may be refused, delaying construction by three months'. Is this appropriate, and why?
options: Yes, because all key threats belong in the PID
Yes, because the approach must show the main risks
No, because specific risks go in the risk register
No, because threats are recorded in the daily log
C.why: The approach describes how risk is managed; it does not contain specific risks, which are recorded in the risk register.

whyNot.0: The PID holds the approach, but specific risks are kept in the register within the project log.
whyNot.1: The approach holds procedures and scales, not the risks themselves.
whyNot.3: The daily log is used for initial risks before the register exists; in initiation the register is set up.

C.q: How does the risk practice support the manage by exception principle, and which role sets the related limit?
options: Risk reviews at stage boundaries; the business layer
Lessons on risk passed on; the project manager
Risk tolerance for aggregated risk; the project board
Risks weighed in the business case; the executive
C.why: Risk tolerance sets limits on aggregated risk and a forecast breach is escalated, applying manage by exception; the board sets risk tolerance from the business's appetite.

whyNot.0: Reviewing at stage boundaries links to manage by stages.
whyNot.1: Passing on lessons links to learn from experience.
whyNot.3: Weighing risks in the business case links to continued business justification.

reteach.title: A fire safety folder
reteach.question: The office has a fire procedure and a list of hazards found in the last inspection. Which is like the approach, and which like the register?

blocks.body: The fire procedure says how hazards are found, rated, reported and who does what: that is like the risk management approach. The list of actual hazards, such as a blocked exit on floor 2 that might cause injury, with who is fixing it and its status, is like the risk register. Writing the blocked exit into the procedure would be in the wrong place.

blocks.text: Specific risks never go in the approach: rules in the approach, risks in the register.

explain.body: How risk will be managed: procedures, techniques, standards and responsibilities. Part of the PID.

test.q: Where should the probability and impact scales for the project be described?
options: In the risk register for the project
In the daily log for the stage
test.why: Scales are part of how risk is managed, so they belong in the risk management approach.

whyNot.0: The register records specific risks, not the rating scales.
whyNot.1: The daily log holds informal issues and notes.
whyNot.2: The business case justifies the project; it does not set rating scales.

explain.body: Specific threats and opportunities, with status and history. Part of the project log.

test.q: Which of these is a risk register heading?
test.why: Risk action owner is a register heading, alongside description, proximity, impact, response and risk owner.

whyNot.1: Appetite is set by the business, not recorded per risk.
whyNot.2: The procedure belongs in the risk management approach.
whyNot.3: Scales belong in the risk management approach.

explain.body: Business: appetite. Board: tolerance and approval of the approach. PM: creates the products and manages risks. Support: maintains the register.

test.q: Who creates the risk management approach?
test.why: The project manager creates the risk management approach in initiating a project; the board approves it.

whyNot.0: The executive, with the board, approves it rather than creating it.
whyNot.2: Project support helps maintain the register; the PM creates the approach.
whyNot.3: Team managers help identify risks in their work packages.

explain.body: Business case weighs aggregated risk; risk tolerance applies manage by exception; stage-end reviews apply manage by stages.

test.q: Checking aggregated risk against the business case supports which principle?
test.why: Aggregated risk feeds the business case, which tests whether the project remains justified.

whyNot.0: Learn from experience relates to lessons on risk.
whyNot.1: Focus on products relates to product definition.
whyNot.3: That principle relates to roles, not checking justification.
